test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 7 July 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If a batsman hits a ball twice other than for the purpose of protecting his wicket or with consent from the opposition then:

options.text: the batsman is given a warning
a bye of five runs is declared

solution:
The correct answer is __**he is out.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A batter is out if h**e strikes the ball twice, **unless he is doing so to** safeguard his wicket o**r with th**e opposition's permission.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **the batsman is given a warning:**

 
 
• The batsman will receive a** first and last warning** if he or she intentionally **damages the pitch.**
 
• Each approaching batsman will r**eceive a warning**, and the warning issued to him will be** valid for the duration of the innings.**
 
 
 
• **the ball is declared dead:**
 
 
• When it is evident to the **bowler's end umpire** that the **fielding side and both batsmen **at the wicket no longer see the ball as in play, it is deemed to be **dead.**
 
• The umpire is the only one who has the authority to determine whether the **ball has been finally settled.**
